title: First night: single-string versus playing rhythm
summary: He felt like a stranger, tried single-string playing, and was told to keep time; he has played rhythm since.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah. So, you went to the William Penn?
And, you began playing with the Basie band?
And, you know, what was that like? I mean, you were walking into a kind of a family.
Right. Right, right, right. Right. Well, that was really something. While -- in the hotel that we stayed in -- I
didn't see anybody, you know. (laugh) The whole day I didn't see --
They were all in their rooms?
Yeah, they were in their rooms, and I wondered -- I said "now -- where is everybody", you know. And, I didn't want to go knock on anybody's door, you know what I mean --
I mean -- just a total stranger.

But then somebody came by, I don't know who it was -- I think Basie probably came by and said "Why don't you come on out tonight"-- you know -- like at the gig. So, I don't know whether I made a rehearsal there at the gig or what. But, I didn't know what to do -- in other words -- I started playing, you know what I mean. I think I was doing some single-string thing, you know. And, which -- that's what I thought, you know, they would like. And, I think Hershel or somebody said "no, no", you know. "Keep some time"-- you know. And, I said "Well, okay". And, I started playing (laugh) -- just keeping time like I, you know, -- I'm accustomed to doing, more or less --
But, I thought that I had to -- you know -- I wanted -- "I don't want to lose this job" -- you know what I mean. I wanted to --
You didn't want them to think that you couldn't deliver something special or something?
Yeah, you know. So, I started playing the rhythm. And I said, "Well, they won't complain to me anymore -- you know -- about the single-string . I'll just play rhythm". And I've been playing
